utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What I'm asking you was or suggesting to you, this forcing or this lack of choice for those people who left in that way was discriminatory, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to force the answer out of me? I don't know whether that is fair. But I try to give you my sincere answer in my previous sentence. I tried to be as sincere as I possibly could.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, are you saying that the circumstances of their leaving, as you've just explained, isn't discriminatory?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that the witness already gave his answer. If you want to force him to give you certain answer that you have in your mind, maybe, I don't know, maybe -- I don't think it's appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I press the question. I've asked the question, a specific part of the question. Mr. Zaric just hasn't answered it. He can answer it but he hasn't. I press that part of the answer. His view was that discriminatory, given in light of all the evidence he's given over the last eight days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but his answer earlier in which he has explained in my view is sufficient. I think it's a question of conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's right. I'm asking him to draw a conclusion based upon what he saw and what he heard. And his experiences there. He's already expressed opinion on other aspects, other things that happened in Samac as being discriminatory. I'm merely asking him in relation to the departures, that's all. It's just another aspect of what he's already agreed to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Well, yes, perhaps he can answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, Her Honour said perhaps you could answer.

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC
utterances.text: Then I'll repeat what I've already stated. I believe that people who had been detained and who had been exposed to all the torture, ill treatment, malnutrition, poor conditions, I believe that those were discriminatory conditions while they were detained. The act of their departure, either through the local or International Red Cross, and the opportunity given to them to say whether they wanted to leave or not, I cannot say that this is an act of discrimination. On the other hand, I fully appreciate the reasons for which the majority of them decided to say no, "I'm not going back to Bosanski Samac."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We shall adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, before we adjourn, just for the record, I don't want to be misunderstood with my comment regarding the issue of the translation. I reiterate again that I'm very grateful to our friends and colleagues from interpreter unit and also court recording, so that there is no misunderstanding there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Yes. The Trial Chamber has been looking at the sitting hours, in view of the medical reports that the Trial Chamber has received, which have been filed and I'm sure the parties have seen them. The Trial Chamber is only asking the parties to sit extended hours for tomorrow, Monday and Tuesday, in order to try and complete the evidence of Mr. Simo Zaric. I'm sure that it's also in his interest to get over with it. So the extended hours will be only with regard to tomorrow, when we are sitting morning and then one and a half hours in the afternoon and Monday and Tuesday. And the break will be half an hour to accommodate the request of the accused persons. That is when we finished sitting at 1345 we will continue our proceedings in the afternoon at 1445 up to about -- 1415 up to about 1545, that is Friday, Monday and Tuesday and hopefully, Mr. Zaric will complete his evidence, including re-examination. We will rise now and continue our proceedings tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: 7.03 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 16th day of May, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.
